---
title: "Poisson Offset–Weight Equivalence"
---

This chapter checks the Poisson identity proved in
@sec-poisson-offset-weight: for a log-link frequency model,

$$
\log\Lambda_i=\log e_i+X_i^\top\beta
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
F_i=N_i/e_i
\text{ with weight }e_i,
$$

where $\Lambda_i=e_i\nu_i$ is the expected count and $F_i$ is the observed
rate. The three LightGBM implementations are:

1. counts + offset via `init_score = log(exposure)`
2. rates + weights via `weight = exposure`
3. a custom objective that injects the offset in the gradients

`predict()` returns a rate for (1) and (2). The custom objective returns a
raw log-rate, so (3) needs `exp`. Set `boost_from_average=False` on the
offset model: the offset already sets the level, and the default would add
$\log\bar N$ on top of $\log e_i$.

```{python}
import lightgbm as lgb
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import poisson

from rich import box
from rich.console import Console
from rich.table import Table

console = Console()
np.random.seed(100)


def _format_value(value: object) -> str:
    """Format scalars for compact terminal tables."""
    if isinstance(value, (np.integer, int)):
        return f"{int(value):,}"
    if isinstance(value, (np.floating, float)):
        value = float(value)
        if abs(value) >= 1:
            return f"{value:,.4f}"
        return f"{value:.6f}"
    return str(value)


def print_table(title: str, df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Render a DataFrame as a Rich table."""
    table = Table(title=title, box=box.SIMPLE_HEAVY, header_style="bold magenta")
    numeric_cols = {col for col in df.columns if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[col])}
    for col in df.columns:
        table.add_column(col, justify="right" if col in numeric_cols else "left")
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        table.add_row(*[_format_value(row[col]) for col in df.columns])
    console.print(table)
```

## Data generation

```{python}
data_easy = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "var1": ["A"] * 5000 + ["B"] * 5000,
        "var2": ["C"] * 2500 + ["D"] * 2500 + ["C"] * 2500 + ["D"] * 2500,
        "expos": np.tile(np.arange(0.1, 1.1, 0.1), 1000),
    }
)

data_mod = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "var1": ["A"] * 5000 + ["B"] * 5000,
        "var2": ["C"] * 2500 + ["D"] * 2500 + ["C"] * 2500 + ["D"] * 2500,
        "expos": np.round(np.random.uniform(size=10000), 4),
    }
)
data_mod = data_mod.loc[data_mod["expos"] > 0].copy()

var_impact = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "var1": ["A", "B", "A", "B"],
        "var2": ["C", "C", "D", "D"],
        "lambda_base": [0.3, 0.7, 1.3, 1.9],
    }
)


def generate_claim_counts(dt: pd.DataFrame, var_impact: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Generate claim counts from exposure × base lambda via Poisson draws."""
    dt = dt.merge(var_impact, on=["var1", "var2"])
    dt["lambda"] = dt["expos"] * dt["lambda_base"]
    dt["claim_count"] = [poisson.rvs(mu) for mu in dt["lambda"]]
    dt["claim_count_adjusted"] = dt["claim_count"] / dt["expos"]
    return dt


data_easy = generate_claim_counts(data_easy, var_impact)
data_mod = generate_claim_counts(data_mod, var_impact)
```

## Solution 1: init_score (counts + offset)

```{python}
def solution_1_predict(data_curr: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Poisson LightGBM with log(exposure) as init_score offset."""
    data_curr_recoded = data_curr[["var1", "var2"]].copy()
    for col in ["var1", "var2"]:
        data_curr_recoded[col] = pd.Categorical(data_curr_recoded[col]).codes

    dtrain = lgb.Dataset(
        data_curr_recoded.values,
        label=data_curr["claim_count"].values,
        init_score=np.log(np.fmax(data_curr["expos"].values, 1e-9)),
        categorical_feature=[0, 1],
    )

    param = {
        "objective": "poisson",
        "num_iterations": 100,
        "learning_rate": 0.5,
        "verbose": -1,
        "boost_from_average": False,  # crucial for offset models
    }

    lgb_model = lgb.train(param, dtrain)
    return np.asarray(lgb_model.predict(data_curr_recoded.values))


predicted_counts_easy = solution_1_predict(data_easy)
data_easy["sol_1_predict"] = predicted_counts_easy * np.fmax(data_easy["expos"], 1e-9)
data_easy["sol_1_predict_raw"] = predicted_counts_easy
predicted_counts_mod = solution_1_predict(data_mod)
data_mod["sol_1_predict"] = predicted_counts_mod * np.fmax(data_mod["expos"], 1e-9)
data_mod["sol_1_predict_raw"] = predicted_counts_mod
```

## Solution 2: Rates with exposure weights

```{python}
def solution_2_predict(data_curr: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Poisson LightGBM on rates with exposure as sample weight."""
    data_curr_recoded = data_curr[["var1", "var2"]].copy()
    for col in ["var1", "var2"]:
        data_curr_recoded[col] = pd.Categorical(data_curr_recoded[col]).codes

    dtrain = lgb.Dataset(
        data_curr_recoded.values,
        label=data_curr["claim_count_adjusted"].values,
        weight=data_curr["expos"].values,
        categorical_feature=[0, 1],
    )

    param = {
        "objective": "poisson",
        "num_iterations": 100,
        "learning_rate": 0.5,
        "verbose": -1,  # boost_from_average=True (default) is correct here
    }

    lgb_model = lgb.train(param, dtrain)
    return np.asarray(lgb_model.predict(data_curr_recoded.values))


data_easy["sol_2_predict_raw"] = solution_2_predict(data_easy)
data_easy["sol_2_predict"] = data_easy["sol_2_predict_raw"] * data_easy["expos"]
data_mod["sol_2_predict_raw"] = solution_2_predict(data_mod)
data_mod["sol_2_predict"] = data_mod["sol_2_predict_raw"] * data_mod["expos"]
```

## Solution 3: Custom objective function

```{python}
def solution_3_predict(data_curr: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Poisson LightGBM with custom objective injecting log(exposure) offset."""
    data_curr_recoded = data_curr[["var1", "var2"]].copy()
    for col in ["var1", "var2"]:
        data_curr_recoded[col] = pd.Categorical(data_curr_recoded[col]).codes

    exposure_values = data_curr["expos"].values

    def custom_poisson_obj(
        y_pred: np.ndarray, data: lgb.Dataset
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        y_true = data.get_label()
        eta = y_pred + np.log(np.fmax(exposure_values, 1e-9))
        mu = np.exp(eta)
        grad = mu - y_true
        hess = mu
        return grad, hess

    dtrain = lgb.Dataset(
        data_curr_recoded.values,
        label=data_curr["claim_count"].values,
        categorical_feature=[0, 1],
    )

    param = {
        "objective": custom_poisson_obj,
        "num_iterations": 100,
        "learning_rate": 0.5,
        "verbose": -1,
        "boost_from_average": False,
    }

    lgb_model = lgb.train(param, dtrain)
    return np.asarray(lgb_model.predict(data_curr_recoded.values))


data_easy["sol_3_predict_raw"] = solution_3_predict(data_easy)
data_easy["sol_3_predict"] = np.exp(data_easy["sol_3_predict_raw"]) * data_easy["expos"]
data_mod["sol_3_predict_raw"] = solution_3_predict(data_mod)
data_mod["sol_3_predict"] = np.exp(data_mod["sol_3_predict_raw"]) * data_mod["expos"]
```

## Analysis: equivalence checks

```{python}
agg_rows = [
    ("Observed counts", data_mod["claim_count"].sum()),
    ("Theoretical counts", data_mod["lambda"].sum()),
]
for i in [1, 2, 3]:
    pred_sum = data_mod[f"sol_{i}_predict"].sum()
    agg_rows.append((f"Solution {i} predicted counts", pred_sum))
print_table(
    "Aggregate Claim Count Comparison (Mod Data)",
    pd.DataFrame(agg_rows, columns=["item", "value"]),
)


equivalence_rows = []
for sol_pair in [
    ("sol_1_predict", "sol_2_predict"),
    ("sol_1_predict", "sol_3_predict"),
]:
    mismatches = data_easy[~np.isclose(data_easy[sol_pair[0]], data_easy[sol_pair[1]])]
    mismatches_mod = data_mod[~np.isclose(data_mod[sol_pair[0]], data_mod[sol_pair[1]])]
    equivalence_rows.append(
        {
            "comparison": f"{sol_pair[0]} vs {sol_pair[1]}",
            "easy_mismatches": len(mismatches),
            "mod_mismatches": len(mismatches_mod),
        }
    )
print_table("Equivalence Checks", pd.DataFrame(equivalence_rows))
```

Each panel plots mean predicted claim count against exposure for one
`(var1, var2)` cell. Black dots are the observed means. Nested markers keep
all three formulations visible where they coincide. They coincide because
the offset, the exposure weights, and the custom gradient share the
estimating equations of @sec-poisson-offset-weight. Every line runs through
the origin with slope $\nu=\lambda_{\mathrm{base}}$, since $\Lambda=e\nu$.

```{python}
solution_styles = {
    "sol_1_predict": ("init_score (counts + offset)", "--", "^", 9, "#0072B2"),
    "sol_2_predict": ("weights (rates x exposure)", ":", "s", 6, "#D55E00"),
    "sol_3_predict": ("custom objective", "-.", "o", 3, "#009E73"),
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 8), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for axis, ((var1, var2), cell) in zip(
    axes.ravel(), data_easy.groupby(["var1", "var2"], observed=True)
):
    observed = cell.groupby("expos")["claim_count"].mean()
    axis.plot(
        observed.index, observed.values, "o", color="black", label="Observed", zorder=5
    )
    for column, (label, style, marker, size, color) in solution_styles.items():
        means = cell.groupby("expos")[column].mean()
        axis.plot(
            means.index, means.values, style, marker=marker, markersize=size,
            color=color, label=label,
        )
    axis.set_title(f"{var1} x {var2} (lambda_base = {cell['lambda_base'].iloc[0]})")
    axis.set(xlabel="Exposure", ylabel="Mean claim count")
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize="small")
fig.suptitle("Exposure scaling: the three Poisson formulations coincide")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
